findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with nodestore data by zip, assuming matching order
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict, and the code does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. There is no guarantee that `events.values()` yields entries in the same order as the input `error_ids`/`node_ids` (get_multi returns results keyed by node id, and any missing entries are absent entirely). When ordering differs or an entry is missing, an error ID gets paired with the wrong event's title/message, so the Seer summary will attribute the wrong error text to the wrong event, and timestamps used for chronological interleaving will be wrong. The lookup should be done by node id (e.g. zip(node_ids, error_ids) and use events.get(node_id)).

findings.title: Error events are merged into every paginated segment page, duplicating error logs
findings.body: The endpoint paginates recording segments with GenericOffsetPaginator and calls analyze_recording_segments(error_events, segments) per page. get_request_data interleaves the full error_events list into each page's logs (error_idx resets to 0 on every call), so a replay whose segments span multiple pages will have the same 'User experienced an error: ...' log lines repeated once per page in the payload sent to Seer. This inflates and distorts the summary. The error events should either be merged only once (e.g. only on the first page, or filtered to the timestamps covered by the current page's segments).

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization branch renders an empty table, discarding all real data
findings.body: In tableResultComponent, when the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag is on, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — hardcoded empty columns and empty data. The actual query results (`result.data`, `result.meta`), loading state, error state, and field aliases are all ignored, so any dashboard table widget for organizations with this flag enabled will render a permanently empty table instead of its data. If this is WIP, the flag must not be enabled for anyone; otherwise the real table results need to be mapped into TabularData/TabularColumn.

findings.title: Reports with neither timestamp nor age pass validation
findings.body: The BrowserReportSerializer marks both `age` (Working Draft) and `timestamp` (Editor's Draft) as required=False, and the cross-field validators only reject the case where both are present. A report containing neither field is accepted and recorded, even though the Reporting API spec requires one of them and the docstring says 'Validate that age is absent, but timestamp is present' (and vice versa). Additionally, the cross-field checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` combined with a timestamp would slip through both validators.

findings.title: Flex justify="right" is not a valid justify-content value
findings.body: The delete-button wrapper was changed to `<Flex justify="right">`. `right` is not a valid CSS justify-content value (valid options include flex-end, center, space-between, etc.), so the justification silently does nothing and the Delete button will not be right-aligned as intended. Use `justify="flex-end"`.
